Thanks, Sanjay — reviewed the usage you sent. A few technical recommendations for the call and for the MAP: 

1) Dedicated pool sizing: base dedicated pool sized for steady-state (~85 qps) + 50% headroom for bursts — gives room for peak Q4 traffic while keeping cost efficient. If you want linear headroom to cover 220 qps peaks, we recommend a two-tier dedicated + burst queue to avoid over-reserving.

2) Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 72 hours → 25% for one week → 100% switch. We’ll include automated rollback and a KV-prefix cache warm-up plan.

3) Latency SLOs: Premium offering can commit to 99th percentile < 250ms for typical generative routes under the dedicated pool with tuned batching. For strict multimodal routes we recommend a per-route SLO and runbook; those will be added to the SLA diff doc.

4) Cost levers: quantization-friendly model flavors and per-route caching could reduce the incremental cost of premium by 8–12% while preserving SLOs. We should validate with a small in-prod spike test.

I’ve attached redwood-premium-sla-diff.pdf with the technical annex and suggested oncall roster. Kicking off commercial modeling once we finalize term and burst capacity shape.
